article.headline: When the Built-In Mac Sleep Guard Runs Out of Options
article.lede: A reply tweet to former OpenAI researcher @willdepue poses a familiar developer question: why install anything when the operating system already ships the tool you need? The answer, in this case, is genuinely nuanced — `caffeinate -imdsu` works well until the laptop lid closes, and on Apple Silicon that turns out to matter a great deal.
article.body:
@abysmal_pepto's reply sits at the intersection of two recent trends: the proliferation of AI coding agents that run for hours unattended, and a cottage industry of macOS utilities built to keep laptops awake while they do. @willdepue, a former OpenAI researcher who contributed to *Sora* and the post-training of several frontier models, had posted about a tool or workflow for preventing a MacBook from sleeping mid-task. The rejoinder: why not use the command already baked into the operating system?

`caffeinate` has lived at `/usr/bin/caffeinate` since OS X Mountain Lion (2012). It works by filing **IOKit power-management assertions** — explicit requests to the kernel not to enter a particular sleep state. The flags in the `-imdsu` combination each address a separate layer: `-i` blocks user-idle system sleep, `-m` blocks disk idle, `-d` blocks display sleep, `-s` blocks full system sleep on AC power, and `-u` briefly declares the user active to wake the display. Run together, they cover every standard sleep pathway except one.

The exception is the one that matters for this conversation. On *Apple Silicon* (M-series) Macs running macOS Ventura or later, closing the laptop lid triggers a hardware-enforced sleep event that `caffeinate` cannot override. Developers running AI agent sessions — extended autonomous tasks in tools like Claude Code or Codex that can run for hours — increasingly want to close the lid and return to a finished result. Neither `caffeinate` nor `pmset disablesleep 1` reliably prevents lid-close sleep on M-series hardware. Apple (AAPL) tightened the power-management stack when it moved to its own silicon, and the assertion model `caffeinate` relies on cannot reach that hardware-level gate. Tools like Modafinil (open-source, narcotic-sh on GitHub) and Amphetamine (free, Apple App Store) were built specifically to address this gap using OS-level APIs that sit above `caffeinate`'s reach.

There are softer limitations too. `caffeinate` is tied to the shell session that launched it: close the terminal window and the process dies silently, sleep prevention gone — unless the user backgrounds it with `nohup caffeinate -imdsu &`. The `-s` flag is explicitly AC-power-only, so on battery it is inert. And the `-u` assertion carries a hard-coded five-second expiry in Apple's open-source implementation; it is designed to simulate a brief user interaction, not hold indefinitely, and while the other flags keep the system awake it means the display-wake component expires quickly.

So the reply deserves a qualified yes. For a developer sitting at a desk, MacBook open, on AC power, who simply wants to prevent the screen from going dark during a build or a long download, `caffeinate -imdsu` is perfectly sufficient — no installation, no permissions, no expanded attack surface. The ecosystem of third-party apps exists for the cases that qualified yes cannot cover: lid closed on Apple Silicon, battery-powered operation where automatic cutoffs matter, non-technical users who need a menu-bar toggle, and anyone who wants expiration alerts or battery-protection rules. The tool is not redundant; it is scoped.

concepts.definition: A request filed by a process to macOS's kernel asking it not to enter a particular power state, such as sleep or display-off. The kernel honors the request as long as the process holds it; when the process exits, the assertion is released. `caffeinate` is the command-line interface for creating these assertions.

Apple's in-house family of ARM-based system-on-chip processors, beginning with the M1 in 2020. Because Apple controls both hardware and software, it can enforce behaviors — such as sleep on lid close — at a level below what the traditional macOS power-management API can override.

A macOS command-line utility for reading and writing power-management settings, such as sleep timers, display-off delays, and the `disablesleep` flag. It operates at a lower level than `caffeinate` but is also constrained by hardware enforcement on Apple Silicon.

A macOS built-in command at `/usr/bin/caffeinate` that prevents the system from sleeping by holding IOKit power assertions. It can be run standalone (holds until the process is killed), with a timeout (`-t`), or tied to another process (`-w <pid>`). Included since OS X 10.8 Mountain Lion.

repos.summary: A Swift menu-bar app for Apple Silicon Macs (macOS 13+) that keeps the system awake even when the lid is closed while allowing the display to turn off. It was built because existing tools including `caffeinate` and Amphetamine could not cleanly handle the lid-close sleep enforcement Apple introduced with its own silicon. The name is a deliberate nod to the naming tradition of caffeinate-adjacent tools (Caffeine → Amphetamine → Modafinil).

ticker_aapl.name: Apple Inc.
ticker_aapl.blurb: Apple designs and markets consumer electronics (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch), software, and digital services. The iPhone remains the dominant revenue driver, but the Services segment — comprising the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay, and licensing — has grown into a high-margin business that Wall Street values separately. Apple commands one of the highest brand loyalty rates in consumer technology and operates a tightly integrated hardware-software ecosystem.
ticker_aapl.recent: Apple reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $400 billion. The company has faced headwinds from slowing iPhone upgrade cycles in mature markets and regulatory pressure on App Store commissions in both the US and EU. Apple Intelligence, its generative AI suite, launched in late 2024 but has not yet materially re-accelerated upgrade cycles. Paul Pelosi sold 45,000 shares of AAPL according to the January 2026 PTR disclosure — the largest single sale in the filing by share count.
